## Summary

I replaced the stub `server.mjs` with a working support ticket MCP server.

### What was wrong
`server.mjs` was a stub: `listTools()` returned `[]` and `callTool()` returned `{content:[]}`, so the existing test failed (`r.content[0].text` was undefined).

### Changes (smallest correct change to `server.mjs` only)
- **`listTools()`** — advertises a single `ticket_create` tool with an explicit JSON schema: `title`/`description` required strings, `priority` optional enum `low/normal/high` with `default: normal`, and `additionalProperties: false` (no extra fields).
- **`callTool(name, args)`** — rejects unknown tools by throwing `Unknown tool: <name>`.
- **`validateCreate(args)`** — enforces the contract:
  - args must be a plain object (rejects `null`/arrays)
  - rejects any field outside `title`/`description`/`priority`
  - `title` and `description` must be present, non-empty (after `trim()`) strings
  - `priority` defaults to `normal`; if provided must be one of the enum values, else rejects
- **Stable sequential ids** — a module-level counter produces `t1`, `t2`, … and the result is a concise text content: `Created ticket t1 "Bug" (normal)`.

The thrown errors integrate with `protocol.mjs`, which already converts thrown errors into JSON-RPC errors (`code: -32602`), so invalid arguments and unknown tools reject cleanly both at the API and over the wire.

### Verification
- Existing test passes (`t1` and `normal` present in result).
- Manually verified all edge cases: unknown tool, missing/blank title, missing description, bad priority, extra field, non-object args.
- End-to-end protocol check confirmed valid calls return results and rejections produce JSON-RPC errors.
- Full test suite (`node --test`): **1 pass, 0 fail**.

The implementation is complete and all tests pass.
